subject: Post-call: hosted SLO alignment, streaming & concurrency clarifications
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@orthohealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@orthohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: hosted SLO alignment, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Hi Alicia / Samir — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.\
\
What we covered (TL;DR):\
- OrthoHealth target: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms for your inference path (end-to-end, client->app->Redwood->app).\
- Typical traffic profile: spikes to 600 QPS sustained for short windows (2–5m), baseline ~120 QPS.\
- Streaming usage: about 35% of requests enable streaming (chunked responses) with average generated length ~240 tokens.\
- Concurrency: front-end maintains 120 concurrent active user connections; burst concurrency to ~420 during busy periods.\
\
Open clarifications we need from OrthoHealth to scope the probe:\
1) Can you share a 10–15 minute sample of production (anonymized) request envelopes (headers + payload size distribution)? We suggested sample_traffic.jsonl.\
2) Are there hard timeouts on your side (client) for streaming chunks? If so, what are they?\
3) Any network middleboxes (WAF/proxy) that add buffering or chunk coalescing? Network trace example.har would help.\
\
Proposed Redwood next steps:\
- Run a hosted quick-probe (non-prod token) that mirrors your envelope for 1 hour to measure end-to-end p95/p99 and identify tail contributors.\
- Provide a short action matrix with recommended batching/cache and a fallback routing policy (hosted -> dedicated fallback).\
- If probe results look good, schedule an engineering 60-min deep-dive to align on rollout guardrails.\
\
Attachments: we attached a template (sample_traffic.jsonl) and a short readme (slo_probe_instructions.pdf) with our recommended probe runbook.\
\
Ask: Alicia — can you share the sample_traffic.jsonl and a network trace (har) by EOD Thursday (2027-11-04)? If you need an anonymization script we can provide one.\
\
Thanks — I’ll loop Ben for the technical probe plan and Karthik for SLO acceptance criteria mapping.\
\
—Lauren\
Lauren Bishop | Account Executive, Redwood Inference\

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@orthohealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orthohealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted SLO alignment, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side:\
\
- We can extract and anonymize a 15-minute sample; will include payload size, call_type (stream vs single), and trace_id.\
- Client-side streaming timeout is 12s for first chunk, then 6s between chunks.\
- We have an edge WAF (CloudEdge) that performs TLS termination and can buffer up to 1s under load; I can ask infra for details and share a capture.\
\
We’ll aim to get the files over by Thursday morning PST.\
\
Also: can you confirm that the hosted probe will include your streaming concurrency behavior (i.e., emulate chunked responses and keepalive connections)? We want the probe to reflect real behavior.\
\
—Alicia
Alicia Torres | Director, Platform Engineering — OrthoHealth
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@orthohealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted SLO alignment, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Thanks for the quick turn, Alicia. Short answers and what we’ll mirror in the hosted probe:\
\
- Yes — we will emulate chunked streaming behavior including first-chunk latency and inter-chunk pacing. We’ll run synthetic clients that hold connections open to model your concurrency shape.\
- We’ll include network-layer variance (jitter) in the probe and, if you provide the HAR, we’ll replay approximate browser edge behavior (TLS handshake timing + buffering).\
\
A few technical asks for the sample so the probe is realistic:\
1) For each sample request: {method, path, payload_size_bytes, is_streaming:true/false, avg_output_tokens}. A one-line JSONL per request is perfect.\
2) If you have a histogram of inter-arrival times (per second buckets) for the 15-minute sample, include it — helps with burst shaping.\
3) Do you enforce rate-limiting at the gateway per-IP? If yes, what thresholds?\
\
We’ll plan a 1-hour probe run on our hosted environment with your envelope and share a replayable runbook (metrics to collect + dashboards). We’ll also produce a short SLO gap table: where hosteds p95/p99 map to your targets and where tooling changes (batching/kvcache/quantization) will materially help.\
\
Putting Karthik on the thread to start drafting the SLO acceptance checklist.\
\
—Ben\
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orthohealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@orthohealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: hosted SLO alignment, streaming & concurrency clarifications

Ben — couple quick operational notes from our infra team that matter for probe shaping:\
\
- We use per-tenant connection pools with a soft-limit of 500 concurrent connections; connection recycling kicks in at 10s.\
- We do not throttle at gateway today but have a circuit-breaker that trips when backend latency > 1.2s for more than 30s.\
\
I’ll attach a small sample trace; Alicia will push the JSONL shortly.\

—Samir
Samir Patel | Staff SRE, OrthoHealth

\
Ben / Karthik — we don’t expect to change client timeouts or gateway behavior during the initial probe; please run the hosted probe against the envelope as-is.\
\
Lauren — suggest scheduling the 60-min engineering deep-dive next week (Nov 9–11). We’re available Nov 10 10:00–11:00 PT.\
\
Thanks — Alicia
